task.title: Trim readings with a slice
task.statement:
This drops the first `warmup` and last `cooldown` sensor readings and returns the middle as a new list. It copies element by element with an index loop — pure Java. You may assume warmup and cooldown are non-negative and warmup + cooldown never exceeds len(readings).

    def trim_readings(readings, warmup, cooldown):
        kept = []
        for i in range(warmup, len(readings) - cooldown):
            kept.append(readings[i])
        return kept

Rewrite it idiomatically in solution.py; same name, same behavior. (Hint: one slice expression, no loop at all.)
task.notes:
Micro-drill. If they ask whether an approach 'counts', say idiomatic means what a fluent reviewer would write today; no other resolutions to give. Targets: index-copy-loop, index-loop.

Idiomatic reference (for your judgment and post-pass debriefs; never hand it over before their run passes):
def trim_readings(readings, warmup, cooldown):
    return readings[warmup:len(readings) - cooldown]
task.appendix:
Targets: index-copy-loop, index-loop

Hidden checks (behavior must be preserved):
assert trim_readings([9, 12, 14, 15, 13, 8], 2, 1) == [14, 15, 13]
assert trim_readings([1, 2, 3], 0, 0) == [1, 2, 3]
assert trim_readings([5, 6], 1, 1) == []
assert trim_readings([4, 8, 15, 16], 1, 0) == [8, 15, 16]
assert trim_readings([], 0, 0) == []
assert trim_readings([7, 7, 7], 0, 2) == [7]

Idiomatic reference:
def trim_readings(readings, warmup, cooldown):
    return readings[warmup:len(readings) - cooldown]

assert trim_readings([5, 6], 1, 1) == []
assert trim_readings([4, 8, 15, 16], 1, 0) == [8, 15, 16]
assert trim_readings([], 0, 0) == []
assert trim_readings([7, 7, 7], 0, 2) == [7]
